Summary Of Job Description

The Senior Project Manager (Sr. PM) assists CAPE in achieving strategic and business objectives by leading project management processes (initiation, planning, executing, monitoring/controlling, and closing) for projects across New Jersey. This Sr. PM role is responsible for both construction and environmental remediation delivery and must be capable of managing field execution, subcontractors, schedules, budgets, safety, quality, and federal documentation requirements.

The Sr. PM integrates all project management knowledge areas (scope, cost, time, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholder management) so the project functions as a cohesive whole. This position serves as a primary point of contact with clients and agencies and effectively leads teams of scientists, engineers, procurement specialists, subcontractors, field personnel, and other stakeholders to meet CAPE’s financial and performance goals.

This role is onsite at active project locations. Not a remote role.

Key Responsibilities

Lead onsite project execution to deliver scope safely, on schedule, and within budget; develop the execution approach, staffing plan, and phased work plan based on scope and risk.
Build and run the Project Management Plan (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholders) and keep plans/baselines current as changes occur.
Control scope using WBS/work packages; manage contract requirements, modifications, and change orders, including impact analysis and timely approvals.
Develop and maintain the integrated schedule (near-term planning through milestones); drive weekly/monthly reporting, corrective actions, and a monthly performance analysis/forecast.
Own project financial performance, cost control, forecasting (ETC/EAC), variance analysis, and recovery plans; identify cost drivers and correct excessive-cost items.
Embed safety and quality into planning and field execution; ensure Safety Plans are in place and followed; maintain incident reporting and a zero-incident culture.
Manage procurement and subcontractors, define and negotiate scopes, oversee performance and invoices, and ensure submittals and progress payments are processed accurately and on time.
Serve as primary client/agency interface (USACE/USEPA as applicable); communicate progress, risks, and issues to stakeholders and executive management; resolve disputes professionally and promptly.
Supervise and lead project staff in accordance with company policies and applicable laws; perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills, Knowledge & Tools

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical procedures, engineering drawings/specifications, and applicable government regulations (including FAR familiarity).
Strong written and verbal communication skills—able to write clear reports/correspondence and confidently present project status, risks, and decisions to stakeholders.
Persuasive communicator with effective negotiation skills; able to develop strong working relationships with executive management, clients, and subcontractors.
Primavera P6 scheduling experience (required/strongly preferred).

Salary

Up to $160,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Travel

50 % on average

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications (Project Manager II) – bachelor’s degree in engineering/science or construction management required. Must have at least three (3) years of progressively responsible related field experience and task management, and two (2) years of onsite Quality Control experience supporting environmental and/or infrastructure work. Must demonstrate a firm grasp of the key project management knowledge areas (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, risk, procurement, communications, stakeholders) as determined by management review.
Senior-Level Requirements (in addition to the above) – Minimum ten (10) years of successful project management experience with emphasis on cost, schedule, communications, and resource management on construction and/or environmental remediation projects. Must have a professional certification (PMP, PE, or PG) and a proven track record delivering complex work (including successfully managing at least two (2) projects over $5M). Must have (or be able to obtain) required field credentials including OSHA 30-Hour Construction and 40-hour HAZWOPER with current refreshers.
Tools / Scheduling – Proficient in Microsoft Office and Windows-based systems; strong ability to develop and maintain project schedules. Primavera P6 experience required (or strongly preferred, depending on your HR “required vs preferred” structure).

Preferred Qualifications

Field experience in construction or environmental projects.

WHY CAPE?

For 35 years, CAPE has delivered construction and environmental remediation solutions to governmental and private organizations nationwide. As a $100 M small business, we have Nationwide contracts with the USACE, USN and USAF totaling over $20 B in prime contract capacity. As a top 3 SB in our industry, our $12 B portfolio also includes unrestricted contracts where we compete against large businesses for task order awards. Most recently in the unrestricted area, CAPE won a $30 M + groundwater treatment plant construction project for the USACE in New Jersey. We routinely partner with other small and large businesses to provide better responsiveness in support of achieving our clients’ goals.

Our projects are high-profile environmental remediation projects involving cleanup of contaminated soil, groundwater, and sediment. The culture of our company is one of working together to achieve our clients’ objectives, company goals and employee’s professional goals and is succinctly and accurately defined as “We, Not Me” behavior. To ensure long-term, sustainable growth, we tailor our 3-year vision to be ahead of our industry in delivering our projects, align with our clients and team partners to improve our existing market share and develop new services to support smart growth.

CAPE offers competitive benefits including Medical/Dental/Vision insurance, life insurance, Vanguard retirement savings plan including both traditional and Roth 401(k) with up to 4% match and lowest in class fees, health savings account (HSA) with investment option, flexible spending account (FSA), paid annual leave, paid maternity/paternity leave, and tuition reimbursement. CAPE also offers staff several other voluntary benefits options, as well as the option to work from home.

The Senior Project Manager will support the successful delivery of TD’s Payments Modernization portfolio, with a primary focus on Modern High Value Payments and related cross-border wires modernization initiatives. This role will lead complex delivery planning, integrated execution, governance coordination, RAID management, stakeholder engagement, vendor coordination, and executive-ready reporting across business, operations, technology, risk, compliance, and vendor partners.

The role requires a strong delivery leader who can operate in a highly matrixed environment, manage multiple releases and dependencies, support TD delivery governance expectations, and help drive disciplined execution across program workstreams. Key Accountabilities

Customer / Business Delivery

Lead planning and execution for assigned Payments Modernization releases, workstreams, and delivery activities, ensuring scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, and decisions are actively managed.
Partner with business, operations, technology, product, risk, compliance, change management, finance, and vendor stakeholders to align delivery expectations and maintain clear ownership across workstreams.
Support Modern High Value Payments delivery activities, including release planning, integration readiness, operational readiness, vendor deliverables, testing coordination, implementation planning, and transition-to-BAU considerations.
Translate complex delivery activity into clear, actionable plans, status updates, escalation materials, and decision-ready recommendations for leadership and governance forums.

Shareholder / Governance, Risk, and Controls

Maintain delivery discipline in alignment with TD governance expectations, including project delivery lifecycle checkpoints, required artifacts, approvals, RAID management, financial tracking inputs, and escalation protocols.
Identify, document, and actively manage risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies, decisions, and change impacts; ensure mitigation plans, owners, due dates, and escalation paths are clearly defined.
Support regulatory, operational, technology, and compliance considerations associated with high-value payments modernization, ISO 20022 enablement, cross-border wires, vendor integration, and platform transition activities.
Prepare materials for working groups, leadership reviews, steering forums, and executive updates, ensuring content is concise, fact-based, action-oriented, and aligned to TD standards.

Employee / Team

Demonstrate inclusive leadership and model TD’s shared commitments by fostering collaboration, transparency, accountability, and respectful challenge across cross-functional teams.
Drive follow-through by ensuring owners, due dates, actions, risks, and decisions are clearly captured, communicated, and tracked to closure.
Support a positive delivery culture focused on execution discipline, continuous improvement, proactive issue resolution, and strong stakeholder partnership.

Depth and Scope

Leads medium-to-high complexity initiatives or workstreams within a large enterprise payments modernization program.
Operates across multiple delivery organizations, jurisdictions, stakeholders, vendors, and impacted platforms.
Requires strong judgment to manage ambiguity, escalate appropriately, and balance delivery speed with governance, risk, control, and operational readiness expectations.
Works independently with limited direction while ensuring alignment with the Delivery Lead, Technology Owner, Business Owner, Product partners, and senior leadership.
Regularly interfaces with senior stakeholders and contributes to governance materials, executive updates, release readiness discussions, and delivery decisioning.

Required Skills And Experience

10+ years of progressive project management or delivery leadership experience, preferably within banking, financial services, payments, technology delivery, or large-scale transformation programs.
Demonstrated experience managing complex projects across business, operations, technology, vendor, risk, compliance, finance, testing, change management, and governance stakeholders.
Strong knowledge of project management disciplines, including integrated planning, milestone management, dependency tracking, RAID management, financial awareness, governance reporting, and executive communications.
Experience working within Agile, waterfall, or hybrid delivery models, including coordination across scrum teams, delivery pods, release plans, and cross-functional working groups.
Strong understanding of payments, wires, high-value payments, ISO 20022, SWIFT, Fedwire, payment operations, or payment processing workflows preferred.
Experience with vendor deliverables, SOW coordination, delivery checkpoints, requirements/design documentation, testing readiness, implementation planning, and production readiness preferred.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce concise leadership updates, meeting materials, action summaries, escalation notes, and decision-ready recommendations.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities, maintain delivery momentum, and drive closure across multiple owners and stakeholders.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, project planning tools, collaboration platforms, JIRA/Confluence, Clarity, and reporting materials used to manage enterprise delivery execution.

Education and Certifications

Undergraduate degree or equivalent experience required.
Project Management Professional (PMP), Agile, Scrum Master, SAFe, or related delivery certification considered an asset.
Payments, banking operations, risk management, change delivery, or financial services transformation experience considered an asset.

TD Leadership and Colleague Expectations

Build deep relationships across business, technology, operations, risk, and vendor partners to support One TD delivery outcomes.
Execute with discipline, urgency, and accountability while maintaining strong risk and control awareness.
Simplify complex delivery information into clear messages, action plans, and decision materials for senior stakeholders.
Do the right thing by owning risks, raising issues early, and ensuring decisions are transparent and well documented.
Win together by fostering collaboration, constructive challenge, inclusivity, and shared accountability across teams.

Who We Are

TD Securities offers a wide range of capital markets products and services to corporate, government, and institutional clients who choose us for our innovation, execution, and experience. With more than 6,500 professionals operating out of 40 cities across the globe, we strive to make every interaction, product and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple. Our services include underwriting and distributing new issues, providing trusted advice and industry-leading insight, extending access to global markets, and delivering integrated transaction banking solutions. new_jobs.description:
What we're doing

Owning a home is a foundational part of building financial security and wealth in America. However, the tools and technology that support homeownership are antiquated, dependent on things like fax machines, handwritten documentation, and hours of manual review.

We're here to change it.

Vesta is the next-generation system of record to power the multi-trillion mortgage market.
We believe that we are overdue for a core transformation – that in order to build a fully automated process and fully digital customer journeys, lenders will have to adopt a system of record platform that is modern, open, and orchestrated by best-in-class software workflows.

Who we are

Our founding team is no stranger to the complexities of the financial industry. As early employees at Blend, they spent years together focused on creating modern cloud infrastructure for banks. Now, with Vesta, they are transforming the mortgage industry by creating the most flexible, open and automated origination experience, benefitting financial institutions and their customers.

And, we're not alone.

We've received $55M in early stage financing from top tier investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Conversion Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and Index Ventures.

We believe that our team is our greatest competitive advantage and take pride in having a team of exceptional humans. As a team, we value humility, empathy, self-awareness, and an orientation towards action. If this sounds like you and you're excited by the idea of getting in at the ground level to be part of building the infrastructure that will power the future of the finance industry, we would love to hear from you!

Who you are

You're looking to join an early-stage team to build something BIG and industry changing. You love coming up with creative solutions to complex problems, working with customers to understand their goals and needs, and managing large scale, enterprise-level projects.

You are deeply customer focused, empathetic, and comfortable advocating for both the needs of the customer as well as the needs of the company. You aren’t intimidated about saying no when necessary to get to the right outcome.

You have experience navigating large scale projects that touch a wide variety of executive, business, and technical stakeholders, as well as experience juggling several different workstreams at a time.

You understand how software is deployed within mature enterprise organizations and you marry that with tight project planning and actioning.

You're a company builder and team player - you're excited to shape and grow the product alongside the culture and operating rhythm of the company.

About the role

As an early implementation manager at Vesta, you'll work closely with the team to:
lead end to end implementation projects with our clients, from sales handoff through user testing and post-go-live, managing multiple stakeholders and critical timelines, all while ensuring we set the foundation for our customers’ ongoing success.
become a Vesta product expert, understanding the nuances of how our product supports our customer’s wide ranging needs, overseeing the configuration and customization of the LOS, and acting as a solutions consultant throughout the implementation lifecycle.
collaborate with cross-functional teams, in particular product, sales, and engineering, to ensure we deliver the right expectations, solutions, and development velocity for our clients.
develop and maintain project documentation, such as project plans, status reports, etc, to help internal and external teams assess progress, next steps, and to help mitigate potential risks and issues.
build strong relationships with our customer stakeholders, acting as a trusted advisor and single point of contact for all implementation related work.

Note: we don't expect you to come in understanding every nuance of the mortgage industry. However, being successful in this role will require a high degree of curiosity and willingness to understand the mortgage ecosystem.

Competitive salary and equity
Robust medical, vision, & dental coverage (~100% of employee premiums are covered)
401(K) plan offering
Meaningful parental leave - 16 weeks fully paid for all new parents, birthing & non-birthing parents (applies to adoptions as well!)
Remote-first culture with a hub in San Francisco
Generous WFH & Wellness Benefits
Monthly Doordash benefits
Open & encouraged flexible time off
Company offsites to get to know the team!

Our cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at $150,000 - $190,000/yr. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.

Marcus Thomas is one of the country’s leading independent advertising and marketing agencies. From our offices in Cleveland and Cincinnati, Ohio; Buenos Aires, Argentina; and Santiago, Chile, we bring together thinkers, makers and storytellers who help brands grow by creating meaningful connections with people.

Cincinnati: Employees in the Cincinnati area work from the Cincinnati office each Wednesday and one additional day per week based on team needs.

Florida, Michigan, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Tennessee and Texas.

About The Role

We are seeking a dynamic and results-driven Project Manager to join our innovative marketing agency. As a Project Manager, you will play a pivotal role in orchestrating and guiding projects from inception to successful execution. You'll collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, leveraging your exceptional organizational, communication and problem-solving skills to deliver exceptional outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Partner with account service and team leads to define project scope, requirements, deliverables and success measures.
Develop and manage project plans, timelines, budgets, dependencies and documentation.
Coordinate team assignments and support resource planning based on project needs and team capacity.
Lead projects from initiation through launch, keeping teams informed and aligned at each stage.
Clarify responsibilities, next steps and deadlines for project team members.
Track progress, identify risks and work with stakeholders to resolve issues before they affect delivery.
Manage changes in scope, priorities, timing and resource needs.
Communicate project status, decisions and concerns clearly to internal teams, clients and other stakeholders.
Support project profitability through accurate budget tracking, resource planning and scope management.
Build productive working relationships across large, cross-functional account teams.
Help teams stay focused and solution-oriented when projects become difficult or priorities change.
Identify opportunities to improve project workflows, documentation and agency processes.

What Success Looks Like

Within 3 Months

Develop a working understanding of the agency, its clients, teams and project management processes.
Build productive relationships with key internal partners.
Learn the agency’s approach to resource planning, including team capacity and project assignments.
Consistently execute assigned work with appropriate support and communicate progress, needs and concerns clearly.

Within 6 Months

Independently manage assigned projects from planning through completion.
Manage project scope, timelines and budgets with limited oversight.
Take ownership of day-to-day resource coordination for assigned work.
Keep teams aligned and respond effectively when project needs or priorities change.

Within 12 Months

Lead more complex projects with confidence and sound judgment.
Identify and support improvements to project management and resource planning processes.
Share knowledge and provide guidance to colleagues when appropriate.
Connect project decisions to client needs, agency priorities and business outcomes.

Required Qualifications

Four to six years of project management experience, including experience independently managing projects from initiation through completion.
Experience managing project scope, timelines, budgets, dependencies and changing priorities.
Experience coordinating cross-functional teams and keeping people aligned around responsibilities, deadlines and decisions.
Ability to work effectively when information is incomplete, priorities are shifting or the path forward isn’t fully defined.
A steady, constructive approach when projects become difficult, with the ability to help teams stay focused and work toward solutions.
Strong communication skills, including the ability to provide clear direction, surface concerns and adapt communication for different audiences.
Ability to ask thoughtful questions, seek context and continue learning when approaching unfamiliar work.
Experience identifying project risks and working with others to develop practical mitigation plans.
Working knowledge of project management practices and tools.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel for budget tracking, reporting and basic data analysis.
Experience in marketing, advertising, creative services, media or another client-service environment, or transferable experience in a similarly fast-paced setting.
Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications (Nice To Have)

These qualifications may help someone ramp up more quickly, but they aren’t required for consideration.

Experience managing projects across multiple channels, such as digital, print, social, broadcast or experiential.
Experience supporting resource planning, including team capacity, assignments and changing staffing needs.
Experience working with large account teams or multiple stakeholder groups.
Familiarity with Workfront, Hive or a comparable project or resource management platform.
PMI, PMP or another relevant project management certification.
Experience improving workflows, documentation or agency processes.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

Long-Term Partnerships: Our clients stay with us for more than 12 years, a reflection of trust and collaboration.
Award-Winning Work: Be part of campaigns recognized for creativity, strategy and results.
Flexibility and Balance: Hybrid schedules and flexible hours support your life and your best work.
Inclusive Culture: Our workplace values every perspective and creates space for all voices.
Growth and Learning: Experience opportunities for professional and personal development through ongoing learning programs.

Benefits Highlights

Time Off: A flexible time-off policy, with most employees taking approximately four to six weeks annually.
Family Support: Twelve weeks of fully paid parental leave.
Health and Wellness: Medical, dental and vision coverage, plus telemedicine, behavioral health resources.
Lifestyle Support: Wellness and creative stipends, phone plan support and partner discounts.
Financial Benefits: A 401(k) with company contributions, student loan repayment support and college savings options.

Team Values

At Marcus Thomas, our values shape how we work with each other and with our clients.

Community: We contribute to the growth of our agency, industry and communities.
Accountability: We keep our commitments and take responsibility for our work and results.
Collaboration: We lead with empathy, listen actively and make room for different perspectives.
Curiosity: We ask thoughtful questions, seek context and remain open to new information and ideas.
Diversity: We respect different identities, backgrounds, experiences and perspectives because they strengthen our teams and our work.
Make Work Play: We bring creativity, energy and enjoyment to the work while respecting that people may express those qualities differently.

Our Hiring Process

Our hiring process is designed to help us learn about your experience and give you a clear understanding of the role, team and agency. The process typically includes an initial conversation with our recruiting team, a hiring manager interview, a team or leadership interview, and final selection.

We use AI-assisted tools to support organization and consistency during parts of the hiring process. Candidates may opt out of recording or transcription at any stage without affecting their consideration for the role.

AI tools don’t make hiring decisions. Members of our recruiting and hiring teams review candidate information and make every decision about who moves forward.

Marcus Thomas provides reasonable accommodations throughout the application and interview process. If you need an accommodation to participate, please contact [email address or contact method]. Requesting an accommodation won’t affect your consideration for the role.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

At Marcus Thomas, we believe different perspectives strengthen our teams and our work. We’re committed to providing fair access to opportunities and creating an environment where employees can contribute, develop and succeed.

We encourage applications from people whose identities and experiences have been historically underrepresented in the advertising and marketing industry, including women, people of color, LGBTQIA+ people, people with disabilities, veterans and people from different cultural, religious and socioeconomic backgrounds.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Axon Community Connect enables public safety agencies to build voluntary, policy-based partnerships with businesses and community members. Through camera registration and secure camera integration, the program expands investigative reach and real-time situational awareness during critical incidents while maintaining privacy, transparency, and camera-owner control.

Working knowledge of hardware, networking, connectivity, and integration concepts—including IP addressing, DHCP, DNS, VLANs, firewalls, ports, Wi-Fi, bandwidth, and basic troubleshooting—and the ability to translate technical findings into clear next steps.

new_jobs.title: Policy Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Policy Program Manager will support the VP, Strategic Policy Management, to manage the function's transition from legacy programs to ICANN's CRM platform and serve as the CRM lead in the function's use of the CRM in day-to-day operations. Working with the Senior Program Manager, the position will act as the primary translator and relationship manager between the function and the organization's Engineering and Information Technology (E&IT) team. The position will be responsible for business requirements gathering, ensuring data integrity during migration, and building the reporting infrastructure needed to measure functional success.
The Policy Program Manager will also work with the Senior Program Manager to manage projects, programs, and operating activities within the Policy Development Support function, to ensure that resources are allocated and prioritized in alignment with the ICANN organization’s strategic, financial, and operating plans.
The role will also represent the function in cross-functional teams for the development, deployment, and maintenance of practical service solutions to support the operations of the Supporting Organizations, Advisory Committees, and community structures serviced by ICANN’s Policy Development Support function and assist the Senior Program Manager with data analysis and reporting as required.
This position will report to the VP, Strategic Policy Management within ICANN's Policy Development Support function.

Key Responsibilities

Managing functional deployment and ongoing administration of the CRM platform, including:
Gathering and defining business requirements, and working with the E&IT team to reflect them in clear technical specifications and user stories
Ensuring data integrity during and after platform migration, cleansing data, and maintaining a robust data governance framework
Change management, including developing and maintaining user manuals and related documentation
Building and publishing reports, metrics, and dashboards to track stakeholder engagement and participation in policy making globally across each of ICANN's Supporting Organizations and Advisory Committeess
Supporting the VP, Strategic Policy Management, and Senior Program Manager to ensure that functional projects and programs are executed in line with available resources and timelines, including developing dashboards and sharing best practices across the function
Other projects and activities as assigned.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)

Experience with Salesforce or other CRM platforms required
Experience with business intelligence, mapping (e.g., Lucid, Visio) and data visualization tools (e.g., Excel, Tableau) required
Data analytics experience a strong plus
Knowledge of Agile/Scrum frameworks and the software development lifecycle a strong plus
Familiarity with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP, e.g., SAP or Oracle) a plus
Strong writing, communication, and presentation skills required
Strong computer skills, including word processing software, spreadsheets, and online collaborative tools (such as Microsoft Office, Google Apps (G Suite), and the Zoom platform) required
Strong organizational and time management skills, demonstrated professional judgement, and proven ability to deliver high-quality work against tight timelines required
Knowledge of ICANN and the domain name industry required
Experience working within a globally diverse team and with emote office environments required
Experience working in international governmental or non-governmental organizations a plus

Education and Experience Requirements

Bachelor's degree in business or a related discipline
Minimum of 8 years' progressive experience in related fields or 5 years’ experience in CRM operations
Certifications demonstrating advanced proficiency with relevant platforms and tools strongly preferred
Project Management Professional (PMP) qualification a strong plus

Working Conditions & Physical Requirements

Remote/flexible location
Ability to travel without restrictions globally, frequently and on limited notice

$82,000 + 10% Bonus + Benefits

Targeted Base Salary High:
$115,000 + 10% Bonus + Benefits

Lam’s Global Quality Team, and a key contributor to achieving Lam’s Quality Vision via successful execution of cross functional Quality programs.

The impact you’ll make

As a Program Manager at Lam, you’re not just overseeing projects, you’re an owner of the key critical quality programs. You'll also be responsible for leading and proliferating 8D program at Lam. 8D is Lam’s primary mechanism for resolving nonconformances registered on products and services. Optimize the design, deployment, execution, and measurement of Lam’s Key Quality Programs.

Influence and enhance Lam's Quality culture by advocating for strong problem solving skills across the organization.
Perform assessments and audits of in-flight 8D records and improve outcomes via coaching or mentoring record owners to a successful resolution, including recurrence prevention across global sites.
Perform data analysis to understand root causes of misses in cycle time completion and below target audit scores; collaborate with stakeholders for solutioning.

12+ years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree, 8 years of experience with a Master’s Degree or 5 years of experience with Ph.D.

Experience as a Project/Program Manager with escalating responsibilities.
Demonstrable abilities in advanced structured problem-solving methodologies (8D, DMAIC, PDCA), Lean Six Sigma, and other established quality tools.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact
Axon Community Connect enables public safety agencies to build voluntary, policy-based partnerships with businesses and community members. Through camera registration and secure camera integration, the program expands investigative reach and real-time situational awareness during critical incidents while maintaining privacy, transparency, and camera-owner control.
As the PSO Program Manager, Community Connect, you will lead the operational health and scalable execution of the Community Connect program across Axon’s U.S. customer base and growing international footprint.
You will establish the operating discipline that enables Program Coordinators to deliver consistent agency outcomes. This includes maintaining visibility into program performance, work-order health, delivery dependencies, technical readiness, and customer-impacting risks; strengthening the processes, tools, and playbooks used across the team; and ensuring complex issues receive the appropriate cross-functional attention.
You will serve as a program-level escalation resource, coordinating with Professional Services, Product, Engineering, Support, Sales, and Finance to remove blockers and drive resolution. You will also provide consultative support for hardware deployment readiness, remote hardware configuration and activation, connectivity, and camera integration requirements.
Your work will enable agencies to launch and sustain Community Connect programs that extend operational visibility, strengthen community participation, and scale responsibly without compromising privacy or the customer experience.
What You’ll Do
Location:
Remote - PT or MT Time Zones

Approximately 30%

Manager, Program Management (Community Connect)

Support work-order management and closure activities, including quality checks, documentation, and internal handoffs.
Serve as a technical resource for deployment planning, hardware readiness, network connectivity, configuration, and integration requirements.
Support the deployment of Cores placed in the field by Community Connect team members, including remote configuration, activation, validation, and onsite technical support when needed.
Troubleshoot hardware, network, connectivity, and video-integration issues; document findings and coordinate escalation with the appropriate technical resources to drive resolution.
Create and maintain technical readiness guidance, deployment checklists, troubleshooting resources, and escalation paths for common Community Connect deployment scenarios.
Develop and maintain playbooks, training materials, job aids, and knowledge resources that enable consistent team execution.
Identify recurring delivery, technical, and process issues; partner with leadership to implement improvements that strengthen program execution at scale.
Support adoption of new products, internal tools, and program updates by ensuring the team has clear guidance and readiness resources.

What You Bring
Bachelor’s degree in program management, project management, operations, information technology, professional services, or a related field; or equivalent practical experience, including 2+ years supporting customer-facing technical deployments, implementations, or professional-services programs involving remote hardware configuration, activation, troubleshooting, and field deployment coordination.
Working knowledge of hardware, networking, connectivity, and integration concepts—including IP addressing, DHCP, DNS, VLANs, firewalls, ports, Wi-Fi, bandwidth, and basic troubleshooting—and the ability to translate technical findings into clear next steps.
Experience managing complex, customer-facing work involving multiple stakeholders, dependencies, risks, competing priorities, and technical escalations.
Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to maintain clear documentation, coordinate across teams, and drive issues through resolution.
Experience developing and improving workflows, playbooks, technical guidance, training materials, and knowledge resources that enable consistent execution.
Proficiency with CRM, project-management, and workflow tools such as Salesforce, Smartsheet, Jira, or similar platforms, as well as Microsoft Office and Google Workspace.
Analytical mindset, with the ability to use data and feedback to identify trends, surface risks, and improve operational performance.
Experience in public safety, SaaS, video technology, physical security technology, connected hardware, or a comparable technical environment is preferred.
Must pass a Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) background check and maintain CJIS clearance.
Ability to handle confidential and highly sensitive information with discretion and sound judgment.

new_jobs.title: Security Manager, Industrial Security & Global Threat Operations
new_jobs.description:
Description

The Leidos Defense Sector has an exciting career opportunity
for an experienced Security Leader
supporting the ILS2 Program in Aiea , Hi
Leidos is seeking an experienced security leader to manage a dual-scope security portfolio: industrial security operations at a secure manufacturing facility supporting DoD, Intelligence Community, and U.S. Government programs, and global threat and crisis management supporting Leidos' personnel, sites, and assets worldwide.

This leader will ensure compliance with 32 CFR Part 117, DoD and IC requirements, and company policy across secure production operations, while also monitoring global threats and leading the organization's response to crises and critical incidents. The role requires close coordination with program management, manufacturing, engineering, facilities, government customers, and Leidos' Global Resilience team — balancing rigorous compliance and risk management with uninterrupted mission and business operations.

Primary Responsibilities

Lead the industrial security program for a secure manufacturing facility, ensuring compliance with 32 CFR Part 117, DoD/IC directives, and customer requirements across production, integration, testing, storage, and shipping.
Oversee physical and personnel security operations, including access control, classified material and CUI handling, clearance actions, indoctrinations/debriefings, and insider threat programs.
Serve as the facility's primary point of contact for DCSA, DoD, and IC security officials; lead preparation for and response to inspections, audits, and reviews, including corrective action closure.
Lead investigations into security incidents and violations, implementing corrective and preventive measures.
Monitor and assess global threats, incidents, and crises affecting Leidos personnel and assets, using threat monitoring and mass notification platforms to support duty-of-care and accountability.
Develop, maintain, and continuously improve business continuity and emergency management plans, while leading and participating in emergency preparedness and tabletop exercises. Incorporate lessons learned and identified gaps into ongoing program improvements. Develop and maintain program-level security policies and procedures, participate in tabletop exercises, and conduct audits and assessments of program security practices to ensure compliance, identify vulnerabilities, and strengthen overall security and operational resilience.
Prepare and disseminate threat assessments, incident communications, and after-action reports for leadership and employees.
Mentor and develop security staff, building a culture of accountability and continuous improvement across both security functions.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree with 8+ years of relevant security experience (industrial security, threat analysis, or crisis management), or a master's degree with 6–10 years; additional experience may substitute for a degree.
FSO, CPSO, or CSSO certification, with experience supporting SAP/SCI programs and knowledge of ICD-705 facility requirements.
Experience with secure manufacturing security, insider threat programs, and DoD manufacturing programs (e.g., U.S. Army).
Working knowledge of emergency preparedness frameworks (NIMS, NRF, ICS); crisis management or FEMA coursework/certification preferred.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience briefing and writing for executive audiences.
Proven ability to manage competing priorities under pressure and tight deadlines; available for extended hours during a crisis.
Must hold a Top Secret clearance with the ability to obtain SCI.

Preferred Qualifications

Strategic, customer-focused leadership with strong judgment and a track record of operational excellence and continuous improvement.
Working knowledge of the Everbridge platform (Suite and Visual Command Center) and OSINT/analytical tools

Job Title:
GSOC and Protective Intelligence Manager

Reports To:
Security Director

FLSA:
Salary / Exempt

Location:
Reno, Nevada

Summary

Under direction of the Security Director, the GSOC and Protective Intelligence Manager will provide oversight and first line management to all GSOC Operations and Intelligence personnel, implement policies and procedures and ensure quality control over all operational support and intelligence production. The GSOC and Protective Intelligence Manager is responsible for communicating GSOC capabilities and processes, as well as Intelligence risk assessments to stakeholders including security customers and C-Suite executives.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Build, lead, manage and motivate GSOC/Intel personnel in a dynamic, rapidly evolving and cross-functional environment that is centered around the use of people, process and technology.
Oversee the development, implementation, and administering of training for the GSOC Operations and Intelligence Teams.
Oversee the hiring, scheduling, supervision and retention of members of the GSOC Operations and Intelligence Teams.
Provide guidance and procedures to the GSOC and Intel Teams to enable their role as the central security data and threat intelligence repository.
Provide guidance for best practices in OSINT collection, Intelligence writing, and reporting for a variety of customers including security agents, security management, and all business offices as requested.
Carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws.
Supervise the implementation of new technologies and business processes to improve efficiency across all security teams.
Complete performance evaluations, provide regular verbal and written feedback to all GSOC and Intel personnel.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Administrative Duties

Inform Security Director on the current threat and risk environment.
Manage Intelligence production calendar and customer requirements.
Monitor Principal family schedules and disposition to guide and assist in coordinating resources.
Coordinate with Security Management on new security technology implementation, maintenance, and functionality.
Provide written guidance documents for Emergency Management and Response, Security Communications, Daily GSOC processes, Information Technology processes, Threat Intelligence reporting, Security Data Management, Security Data Integrity and Availability, Security Systems Protection.
Monitor timecards, credit card purchases, and scheduling to ensure appropriate compliance and staffing coverage within the GSOC Operations and Intelligence Teams.
Maintain complete inventories of all GSOC contracts, office equipment, and communication equipment.
Manage security petty cash distribution/documentation for accounting.
Review vendor invoices and manage vendor relationships.

Liaison

Coordinates with the Security Director, residential security, physical security EP, IT, security contract vendors and internal staff to accomplish common goals and promote company vision, purpose and values.
Attends Security Management and cross-team meetings.
Maintains effective liaisons with the Human Resources Department to ensure proper protocols and support to team members are provided.
Create and maintain relationships with all company departments to promote their utilization of GSOC and Intelligence capabilities.
Coordinate with the CyberSecurity Team on overall Risk Assessments, promotion of CyberSecurity awareness, and GSOC adherence to CyberSecurity best practices.
Maintain professional and productive relationships with GSOC vendors and ensure timely implementation, training, renewals, payments, and changes to contracts.
Support the company Business Continuity Plan by maintaining proper notification directories and a redundant Operations Center in the case of a GSOC outage.

Project Management

Identify opportunities for GSOC and cross-functional collaboration and efficiencies by maintaining current knowledge of industry best practices and tools.
Identify, Assess, and coordinate implementation of new technologies and capabilities with the IT and CyberSecurity Teams.
Coordinate and oversee progression of Objectives and Key Results deadlines for Security Annual Operating Plan (AOP).
Complete projects as assigned.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education/Experience

Candidate should have a minimum of:

Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university, or equivalent combination of education and experience
6+ years in corporate security, military intelligence, or emergency management, with 3+ years in a leadership role.
Experience in Intelligence analysis, writing, and production.
Experience in project management and implementation of new technologies across multiple teams.

Knowledge/Skills And Abilities

Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills.
Ability to think and act strategically and proactively.
Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals.
Ability to effectively present information and respond to requests from executives, managers, clients, and staff.
Able to analyze complex situations and recommend solutions.
Able to manage multiple projects simultaneously with competing priorities and deadlines.
Protection of confidential business information.
Advanced knowledge of Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) best practices.
Experience with investigations and intelligence collection.
Basic knowledge of Cyber Security, Information Technology, and/or Network Security.

Computer Skills

Position requires proficiency using the Internet, email, MS Office and Google Drive.
Understanding of data privacy and security and how to implement safeguards for confidential information.

Working Conditions

Able to work irregular or extended hours.
Able to regularly stand, walk, sit, use hands/manual dexterity, reach or stretch, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; speak or hear.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.
Specific hearing required by this job include ability to hear and understand phone and radio transmissions.
Exposure to sensitive and confidential information.

Salary And Benefits

Base salary $205k-$220k
Paid sick leave
Paid time off (PTO) accrual
Holiday pay for select holidays
Company 401(k) employer match
Medical, dental and vision coverage for the employee + their dependents
Health reimbursement arrangement
529 scholarship match
Paid time off for volunteer work
Yearly bonus program
Life insurance policy

new_jobs.description:
Vacature kenmerken

Standplaats: Den Helder

Contractduur: 2 jaar

Uren per week: 36 - 40

Maandsalaris: €3.674,00 - €5.863,00

Salarisniveau: Burgerschaal IBBAD 10 - Burgerschaal IBBAD 10

Niveau: HBO Bachelor

Vakgebied: Orde / vrede / veiligheid

Vacaturenummer: 75286

Dienstverband: Tijdelijke aanstelling met zicht op vaste aanstelling

Functiegroep: Burger

Functieomschrijving

Ben je van nature iemand die initiatief toont? Een uitdaging niet uit de weg gaat? Haal je gemakkelijk belangrijke details uit grote hoeveelheden informatie en leg je makkelijk verbanden? En heb je een passie voor het creëren van veilige omgevingen en het beschermen van wat ons dierbaar is? Dan past de functie Security Manager
helemaal bij jou!

Dit ga je doen

Impact op vrede en veiligheid in Nederland en ver daarbuiten, die heb je zeker als Security Manager
bij de Koninklijke Marine. Je zorgt dat onze eigen mensen en middelen beschermd zijn tegen fysieke dreigingen.

Als Security Manager bij Defensie ben jij de spil in het waarborgen van de weerbaarheid van Defensie. Jij zorgt ervoor dat onze organisatie niet alleen dreigingen afweert, maar ook proactief inspeelt op nieuwe uitdagingen. Je bouwt mee aan een cultuur waarin veiligheid en flexibiliteit centraal staan, zodat het CZSK altijd effectief kan blijven opereren – ook bij onverwachte situaties. Door het borgen van weerbaarheid van Defensie zorg je ervoor dat wapensystemen, infrastructuur en informatiesystemen beschermd en inzetbaar blijven. Kortom, je draagt bij aan de inzetbaarheid en slagkracht van de Koninklijke Marine!

Het mooie aan jouw functie is dat je verantwoordelijk bent voor het borgen van fysieke en personele beveiliging binnen het CZSK, maar ook als Subject Matter Expert in dit domein. Daarnaast ook het adviseren
bij voorstellen en het implementeren maatregelen tot het vergroten van beveiligheidsbewustzijn onder collega’s. Je adviseert de commandant en werkt nauw samen met andere afdelingen en security experts. Zo ben jij een van dé verbindende schakels binnen het beveiligingsnetwerk van de Koninklijke Marine.

Werken voor Defensie, maar niet als militair? Dat kan! Naast circa 41.000 beroepsmilitairen werken er nog zo'n 20.000 burgermedewerkers bij Defensie. Als burgermedewerker draag je geen uniform, maar werk je wel vanuit je eigen vakgebied wereldwijd mee aan vrede en veiligheid. En je krijgt de unieke kans om je vakkennis te verdiepen, de dynamische wereld van Defensie te ervaren én intensief samen te werken met onze militairen. Zo maak je jouw specialisme nog specialer.

De Security Manager
is verantwoordelijk voor het borgen van fysieke en personele beveiligingsmaatregelen binnen de CZSK organisatie door het vertalen van het DBB naar de praktijk. In deze rol zorgt de Security Manager ervoor dat het Defensie beveiligingsbeleid wordt nageleefd, geeft advies aan leidinggevenden, commandanten (en zijn/haar security organisatie) over beveiliging en risico’s binnen het werkgebied.

Adviseert en ondersteunt de commandanten en hoofden van eenheden, afdelingen en instellingen en hun beveiligingsfunctionarissen m.b.t. de uitvoeringsmaatregelen op het gebied van personele en fysieke beveiliging.
Coördineert de implementatie van beveiligingsmaatregelen op het gebied van personele en fysieke beveiliging.
Stemt de maatregelen inzake personele en fysieke beveiliging en de uitvoering daarvan binnen CZSK af met het bureau beveiligingsautoriteit, de beveiligingsfunctionarissen van de andere Defensieonderdelen, de Dienst Vastgoed Defensie en het stafbureau INFRA van CZSK.

Functie-eisen

Opleiding:

Vereist:

Een afgeronde HBO beveiligingsopleiding op het gebied van integrale beveiliging of een HBO opleiding die hier nauw bij aansluit, of aantoonbaar HBO denkniveau aangevuld

Ervaringseisen
:

Voorkeur voor ervaring op het gebied van personele en fysieke beveiliging opgedaan als Beveiligingsfunctionaris of binnen een stafbureau bij een organisatie onderdeel binnen Defensie. Voor de functie is het noodzakelijk over een Verklaring van Geen Bezwaar (VGB) te beschikken. Heb je deze niet, dan wordt deze aangevraagd voordat tot definitieve aanstelling wordt overgegaan.

Arbeidsvoorwaarden

Salarisniveau: Burgerschaal IBBAD 10 - Burgerschaal IBBAD 10

Salarisomschrijving: Het salaris is gebaseerd op een 38-urige werkweek.

Maandsalaris: €3.674,00 - €5.863,00

Dienstverband: Tijdelijke aanstelling met zicht op vaste aanstelling

Contractduur: 2 jaar

Maximaal aantal uren per week: 40

Overige arbeidsvoorwaarden

Naast het salaris ontvang je een Individueel Keuzebudget (IKB). Het IKB bestaat uit geld (16,33% van je bruto jaarsalaris) en tijd. Met het IKB maak jij de keuzes die bij jou passen en kun je een deel van je arbeidsvoorwaarden zelf samenstellen. Je kunt er bijvoorbeeld voor kiezen om een deel van je maandinkomen te laten uitbetalen wanneer jij dat wenst. Ook kun je dit budget omzetten in verlof en andersom of besteden aan fiscaal vriendelijke doelen. De Rijksoverheid hecht sterk aan persoonlijke groei en loopbaanontwikkeling en biedt daarvoor tal van mogelijkheden. Tot de secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden behoren onder meer verschillende studiefaciliteiten, bedrijfsfitness, volledige vergoeding van je OV-reiskosten woon-werkverkeer en gedeeltelijk betaald ouderschapsverlof.

Tot slot bieden we je iets wat veel andere werkgevers niet kunnen: de kans om bij te dragen aan vrede en veiligheid wereldwijd.

Bijzonderheden

Organisatieomschrijving

Defensie zet zich in voor de belangen, welvaart en vrijheid van Nederland. We zijn dagelijks actief in binnen- en buitenland. Onze wereldwijde inzet versterkt de internationale samenwerking en zorgt ervoor dat mensen zich in vrijheid kunnen ontplooien. Nu en in de toekomst.

Bij het ministerie van Defensie werken ongeveer 79 duizend mensen direct en indirect aan vrede en veiligheid. Het ministerie bestaat uit het Commando Materieel & IT (COMMIT), de Bestuursstaf (het departement), de Koninklijke Marine, de Koninklijke Landmacht, de Koninklijke Luchtmacht, de Koninklijke Marechaussee, het Defensie Ondersteuningscommando (DOSCO).

Defensie is een van de grootste werkgevers van Nederland en vertoont overeenkomsten met een groot bedrijf. De operationele commando's (zee-, land- en luchtstrijdkrachten), de Marechaussee, het DOSCO en de COMMIT lijken op werkmaatschappijen.

new_jobs.title: Technical Project Manager, Integrations
new_jobs.description:
The Role

Beacon acquires vertical market software companies and brings them onto a common operating standard. Integration is the function that runs the window between close and steady state, coordinating IT, Finance, GTM, Legal, and HR so that a newly acquired company lands cleanly rather than by improvisation.

You will run that window. Each integration is a fixed, fast-moving program with a defined start and a defined handoff, and you will be the person holding the plan, the cadence, and the escalations across every function involved. This is a hands-on role. You will drive the plan and you will do work inside it.

What You'll Do

Run integrations from close to handoff.
Own the integration plan for each acquisition: scope, sequencing, owners, and dates across every function. Drive the recurring cadence, keep the plan current, and land the handoff on time.

Be the coordination point for the acquired company.
Work directly with the GM and their team through their first weeks inside Beacon. Translate between how they operate today and how Beacon operates, and make sure nothing lands on them twice or not at all.

Move companies onto the Beacon standard.
Identity, devices, security baselines, and core business systems. You will partner with IT, Security, and the systems owners to sequence the migrations and to unblock them when they stall.

Hold the line on status.
Report progress honestly to leadership, including the parts that are behind. Escalate early and with a recommendation attached rather than late and with a surprise.

Run and sharpen the playbook.
Each integration should be faster and cleaner than the last. Find the steps that keep breaking, fix them in the playbook, and make the improvement stick across the next one.

Required

5+ years in project or program management, running cross-functional programs end to end
Experience coordinating across IT, Finance, GTM, Legal, and HR, or an equivalent set of functions with competing priorities
Comfort with technical systems: identity, device management, and core SaaS platforms. You do not need to configure them, but you need to follow the work and ask sharp questions
Experience building process, templates, and structure where none existed
Strong written communication. Much of this job is a clear status update landing in the right inbox at the right time
A bias for action. You would rather move something forward than perfect the plan
The agility to adapt when a program changes shape mid-stream, and the confidence to get hands-on when it needs you

Nice to Have

Post-close M&A integration experience, in-house or in advisory
Exposure to IAM, MDM, or SSO rollouts
Exposure to SOC 2, ISO 27001, or SOX ITGC programs
Automation experience
A habit of spotting the smarter way to do something and then doing it

Our Values at Beacon Software

Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.
Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.
Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.
Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.

How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process:
To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Beacon Software uses Artificial Intelligence and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions:
Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

new_jobs.title: Technical Project Manager, Integrations
new_jobs.description:
The Role

Beacon acquires vertical market software companies and brings them onto a common operating standard. Integration is the function that runs the window between close and steady state, coordinating IT, Finance, GTM, Legal, and HR so that a newly acquired company lands cleanly rather than by improvisation.

You will run that window. Each integration is a fixed, fast-moving program with a defined start and a defined handoff, and you will be the person holding the plan, the cadence, and the escalations across every function involved. This is a hands-on role. You will drive the plan and you will do work inside it.

What You'll Do

Run integrations from close to handoff.
Own the integration plan for each acquisition: scope, sequencing, owners, and dates across every function. Drive the recurring cadence, keep the plan current, and land the handoff on time.

Be the coordination point for the acquired company.
Work directly with the GM and their team through their first weeks inside Beacon. Translate between how they operate today and how Beacon operates, and make sure nothing lands on them twice or not at all.

Move companies onto the Beacon standard.
Identity, devices, security baselines, and core business systems. You will partner with IT, Security, and the systems owners to sequence the migrations and to unblock them when they stall.

Hold the line on status.
Report progress honestly to leadership, including the parts that are behind. Escalate early and with a recommendation attached rather than late and with a surprise.

Run and sharpen the playbook.
Each integration should be faster and cleaner than the last. Find the steps that keep breaking, fix them in the playbook, and make the improvement stick across the next one.

Required

5+ years in project or program management, running cross-functional programs end to end
Experience coordinating across IT, Finance, GTM, Legal, and HR, or an equivalent set of functions with competing priorities
Comfort with technical systems: identity, device management, and core SaaS platforms. You do not need to configure them, but you need to follow the work and ask sharp questions
Experience building process, templates, and structure where none existed
Strong written communication. Much of this job is a clear status update landing in the right inbox at the right time
A bias for action. You would rather move something forward than perfect the plan
The agility to adapt when a program changes shape mid-stream, and the confidence to get hands-on when it needs you

Nice to Have

Post-close M&A integration experience, in-house or in advisory
Exposure to IAM, MDM, or SSO rollouts
Exposure to SOC 2, ISO 27001, or SOX ITGC programs
Automation experience
A habit of spotting the smarter way to do something and then doing it

Our Values at Beacon Software

Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.
Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.
Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.
Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.

How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process:
To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Beacon Software uses Artificial Intelligence and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions:
Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

If you are ready to build a world-class consumer experience that genuinely rebuilds American communities, come build with us.

About The Role & Your Impact

We're looking for a Business Operations Analyst, Planning to own Zero's view of the future: what we'll sell, what we can deliver, and what we need to deliver it. Reporting to the Sr. Manager of Business Operations, you'll build the demand forecasts and capacity plans that determine where we put our people, our contractor capacity, and our capital.

This is not a spreadsheet-maintenance role. It's a thinking role that requires a deep understanding of the underlying business. Every market has its own demand curve, its own programs, and its own contractor bench, and getting thousands of projects a week means keeping demand and supply in balance across all of them. Your job is to see the constraint before it finds us, put a number on it, and give leadership a plan they can act on.

What You'll Bring

Demand Planning

Own the demand forecast by market, channel, and program, built from real drivers: lead rates, close rates, install rates, and signed backlog.
Incorporate the levers that move volume: pricing, marketing spend, advisor staffing, program launches, and new market entry.
Monitor leading and lagging indicators to assess performance against plan, and flag when the forecast, or the modeling logic itself, needs to change.
Proactively manage short- and long-term growth targets, with clear reporting to leadership on how we're tracking.

Supply & Capacity Planning

Translate demand into supply requirements: contractor install capacity by market, and equipment quantities and timing.
Find the constraint before it finds us: know where capacity, equipment, or program funding will bind next, and quantify what it costs us.
Model capacity and readiness for new markets, programs, and product launches so we commit with our eyes open.
Partner with Fulfillment and Supply Chain to keep the plan grounded in what our contractor network and distributors can actually absorb.

Sales & Operations Planning

Run the S&OP cadence that reconciles demand, capacity, and procurement across Sales, Fulfillment, and Finance.
Surface risks and propose solutions to leadership; you own the forecast, which means you own the miss, not just the spreadsheet.
Partner with Finance on scenario analysis for our biggest decisions: new markets, pricing changes, program participation, and growth investments.

Planning Systems & Data Foundations

Build a modern, AI-enabled planning stack: automate models to improve accuracy and kill manual work as the business scales.
Document forecast methods, assumptions, and drivers so plans are transparent and reproducible.
Leverage AI tools to compress the time between question, model, and answer.

What You Bring

2-5 years in supply/demand planning, business operations, consulting, or a data-heavy analytical role, ideally at a high-growth company.
Deep analytical horsepower: you're rigorous with numbers (ideally with a formal math background), fast in spreadsheets, and skeptical by default.
Comfort managing a high degree of complexity across markets, programs, and product lines without losing the thread.
Business sense beyond the numbers: you understand how funnels, field operations, and physical capacity actually work.
Structured communication skills: you can present a plan to leadership, defend your assumptions, and land a recommendation.
Accountability for a forecast: you'd rather be honestly wrong and recalibrate than vaguely right.
You've AI-enabled yourself to move fast across whatever stack you land in.

Nice to Have

Experience in home services, energy, construction tech, marketplaces, or businesses with physical operations.
Experience with demand forecasting, capacity planning, or S&OP.
Familiarity with SQL, Python, or R for analysis.
Experience supporting annual planning, budgeting, or board-level planning materials.

About This Position

ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION

Over 51 million passengers traveled through Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) in 2025, one of the busiest airports in the country in the nation's 5th largest city. Phoenix Sky Harbor is the commercial air service airport and the largest of three airports in the Phoenix Airport System (Phoenix Sky Harbor, Deer Valley, and Goodyear airports), which is managed and operated by the City of Phoenix Aviation Department. Phoenix Sky Harbor serves more than 142,000 daily passengers with over 1,300 flights per day, served by 24 airlines with nonstop air service to over 140 destinations, including 25 international markets. Phoenix Sky Harbor has a total economic impact of more than $44.3 billion per year.

About The Division

The City of Phoenix Aviation Department is seeking a results-oriented professional to serve as the Concessions Program Manager within the Business and Properties Division at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX). The Aviation Business & Properties Division is comprised of four (4) section teams: (1) Airline & Agency Affairs; (2) Concessions; (3) Parking Services & Rental Car Center; and (4) Commercial Properties. This division is responsible for the management of the business relationship with airline tenants and aviation agency affairs, and revenue generation through the concessions program; airport parking facilities and rental cars; commercial property leasing and property management, and airport real estate land development. Collectively, these sections are responsible for a revenue portfolio totaling approximately $580 + million annually.

About The Position

The City of Phoenix Aviation Department is seeking a results driven professional to serve as the Concessions Program Manager within the Business and Properties Division at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport. This role supports the development, execution, administration, compliance oversight, and stakeholder coordination for the airport's Concessions Program, which includes Food & Beverage, Retail, and Passenger Services. The position manages staff by providing leadership, direction, training, mentoring, and development opportunities. Responsibilities include researching and identifying new revenue opportunities; analyzing lease terms; assessing space needs; and evaluating tenant requests.

The Concessions Program Manager will engage with corporate level tenants, present proposals on customer and tenant issues, and lead lease negotiations. The role oversees team compliance with contracts, agreements, leases, and permits, and prepares written reports and presentation materials for various audiences. It also provides recommendations and serves as project owner for Tenant Improvement Projects within the assigned section, and conducts benchmarking with other large commercial airports.

This is a professional supervisory position requiring independent judgment, excellent interpersonal skills, the ability to maintain professionalism and diplomacy at all times, business writing and presentation skills, critical thinking, financial and statistical data interpretation, and experience in contract leasing negotiation. The selected candidate will be required to operate in a fast-paced airport business environment, handling a variety of projects concurrently and engaging with tenants extensively.

Core Job Duties

Oversee concession contracts, including food and beverage, retail, and passenger services, ensuring compliance with agreement terms and optimizing revenue opportunities.
Conduct research and provide recommendations to support the commercial development of airport concessions.
Administer and ensure compliance with concession lease agreements by monitoring operator performance and resolving issues.
Assist with drafting proposals and lease documents, helping ensure accuracy and alignment with procurement and airport requirements.
Assist the Concessions Superintendent with writing the concessions contract scope of work for procurements.
Recommend evaluation criteria for proposals to division leadership and support the competitive selection process.
Develop and recommend plans and budgets to support concession program operations and revenue goals.
Monitor and analyze sales reports, financial performance, and revenue trends to identify risks, opportunities, and areas for improvement.
Conduct research and provide recommendations to support the commercial development and long-term planning of airport concessions.
Deliver presentations to City officials, airport boards, airport tenants, department executives and senior leadership, and community groups regarding airport concessions programs.
Working extended and irregular hours outside of Monday - Friday 7 am to 6 pm, including nights, weekends, and holidays, may be required based on airport event activity and/or emergency airport events. This may equate to more than 40 hours in a workweek without additional compensation.

IDEAL CANDIDATE

Stakeholder Engagement & Relationship Building
Demonstrated ability to cultivate and maintain strong relationships with internal teams, external stakeholders, tenants, concessionaires, customers, and governmental agencies.
Skilled in navigating diverse interests and maintaining trust in a complex, high visibility environment.

Communication Excellence
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly and effectively at all organizational levels.
Ability to develop clear, concise, and compelling reports and presentations tailored for diverse audiences, including executive leadership and elected officials.

Collaboration & Consensus Building
Ability to work cross-functionally and align diverse interests to develop consensus on complex issues.
Demonstrated success in facilitating discussions that balance stakeholder needs with organizational goals.

Operational Agility
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and respond effectively to changing conditions, while maintaining program momentum in a dynamic airport environment.
Ability to lead, motivate, and coordinate cross functional teams while fostering collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Industry & Regulatory Expertise
Experience with the strategic development of competitive requests for proposals processes necessary to implement a concessions program.
In-depth knowledge of FAA policies, principles, and regulatory procedures regarding airport concessions and non-aeronautical revenue programs.
Knowledge of airport concessions development, negotiations, procurement processes, and contract management.

Analytical Thinking & Data-Driven Business Acumen
Strong analytical skills with a data-driven approach to evaluating financial performance, identifying trends, and supporting strategic decision making.
Proficiency in research methods, benchmarking, and applying insights to enhance program performance and commercial outcomes.

Diplomacy and Discretion
Ability to exercise tact, discretion, and sound judgment when handling sensitive and confidential matters.
Skilled at navigating complex issues with professionalism and maintaining positive working relationships.

Demonstrated ability to build and maintain professional relationships with concessions tenants, legal counsel, and internal department team.
